💡 First demonstration of Sn(BF4)2/H2O additive in non-flammable TMP-ethanol organic electrolyte, creating a gradient/bilayer SEI on Zn anodes via solvent-salt-metal synergy (Sn coating, BF4-derived interphase, H2O proton source). This enables 7000 h durability, 10 mA cm−2 rate capability, and 99.8% CE, offering a rare additive strategy to boost stability and lifespan of non-aqueous Zn batteries.

💡 The novelty lies in covalently grafting a Schiff-base-functionalized UiO-66-NH₂ MOF onto the Zn anode to create a bifunctional interface combining chemical chelation (accelerating desolvation, suppressing side reactions) with confined pore channels guiding uniform Zn²⁺ flux and Zn(002)-oriented deposition. Significance: achieves 99.8% Coulombic efficiency over 2000 cycles and >90% capacity retention after 4000 cycles, advancing stable aqueous zinc-ion batteries.

item.title: Chemically Reactivatable Sulfide Interfaces for Low‐Pressure Thick‐Cathode Solid‐State Na–S Batteries
item.description:

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in Fe3C–MnO heteropoints embedded in N-doped hollow carbon nanotubes that chemically reactivate sulfide interfaces, suppressing passivation and sustaining sulfur recovery under weak mechanical confinement. This decouples reversible sulfur chemistry from high-pressure requirements, cutting operational pressure from ~2 MPa to 0.2 MPa while enabling thick cathodes (8.3 mg cm−2) and 696 Wh kg−1 pouch cells—significant for practical low-pressure solid-state Na–S batteries.
🏷 solid-state Na-S battery · thick sulfur cathode · Fe3C-MnO heterojunction · sulfide interface · low-pressure operation

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in converting crystalline cyclo-Se8 into amorphous submolecular Sex (x<4) on graphene, boosting conductivity and Li+ diffusivity, plus a Li2O-nanoshell sulfide electrolyte stabilizing interfaces. Significance: enables low-pressure (2.5–8 MPa), recyclable all-solid-state Li–Se batteries with 673 mAh g−1, 2800-cycle stability, −30°C operation, and 420 Wh kg−1 pouch cells.

💡 The review innovatively establishes a comprehensive framework spanning microscopic mechanisms to macroscopic system-level protection for lithium-ion battery thermal safety.
